sections.h2: Is a cash sale the best way to leave a Greenville house quickly?
sections.html:
Often it is, since no lender's appraisal stands between you and the closing date. A regular listing can still work if the home is in good order, though you will prep it and sit through showings.

Greenville is the Hunt County seat, about sixty miles northeast of Dallas on Interstate 30, so buyers come from a smaller pool than in the inner suburbs. A house that sits on the market for months can pick up carrying costs: taxes, insurance, utilities and mowing. Weigh those against the lower price a cash buyer may offer.

  • Agent listing: suits an updated house and a flexible schedule.
  • Private sale: suits owners who can manage contracts and disclosures.
  • Cash offer: suits a vacant house, an estate property or one with deferred repairs.

sections.h2: What should sellers know about Greenville and Hunt County?
sections.html:
Greenville was established in 1846, the same year the legislature created Hunt County, and the town takes its name from a Texas general. The Texas State Historical Association says residents chose a 640-acre prairie site donated by a surveyor, and the city incorporated in 1852. The blackland soil around town made it a cotton market, and railroads arrived between 1880 and 1896.

The city has a record of firsts in public services. In 1891 its government began running an electricity plant, which the state history calls the first municipally owned utility system in Texas. Aircraft work took over after World War II: a wartime airfield called Majors Field later hosted overhaul and defense electronics operations, and the state history names the defense electronics firm there as the city's largest employer.

Roads shape the map. Interstate 30, U.S. highways 380, 69 and 67, and State highways 224, 66 and 34 all pass through, and three railroads cross town. The population was 23,960 in 2000 after peaking near 27,750 in 1990. Annual events include the Hunt County Fair in August and the Cotton Pickin' Arts and Crafts Jubilee in November.

Older homes close to the downtown square date from the era of the cotton boom and wartime expansion. Whatever the age of your house, a folder of receipts for roof, plumbing and electrical work gives a buyer something concrete to read.

sections.h2: How did Greenville's growth shape its neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Growth came in waves, and each wave left housing behind. The town counted about 3,000 people in 1884, roughly 5,000 by 1892 and 14,000 by 1914, helped by rail lines and a cotton trade that shipped over $1 million of cotton a year in the early 1890s. Streetcar service even reached a college campus in 1912.

Between 1933 and 1952 the population rose from 12,407 to 14,697, and during 1941 and 1942 the city issued $60,000 in bonds to buy and improve 760 acres for a wartime airfield. An aircraft overhaul company leased part of that field in 1951, started with 400 workers, and by the late 1960s a successor employed 4,600. Houses built for that workforce are now several decades old and may carry original wiring, plumbing and roofs.

If your property dates from one of those periods, say so in your listing or your conversation with a buyer, and ask Hunt CAD for the year-built on its record so your description matches.

sections.h2: What do Greenville property taxes look like for an owner?
sections.html:
The Hunt County Appraisal District, known as Hunt CAD, appraises all real and business personal property in the county, and the county tax assessor-collector sends the bill. The district's site offers online property search, a homestead exemption portal and a truth-in-taxation tool, and it warns owners not to pay anyone a fee to file a homestead application because the district charges nothing.

Texas has no state property tax. County, city and school district each set a rate for your house, while the appraisal district assigns the value as of the first of January. Bills mail around October 1. Per the Comptroller, a balance still open on February 1 becomes delinquent and starts drawing penalty and interest.

Hunt CAD's home page notes that requests such as property splits or combines made after April 1, 2026 apply to the 2027 tax year. That kind of cutoff is worth knowing if you are dividing a tract before a sale.

  • Protests are usually due May 15, unless your notice arrived late enough to extend the window.
  • After the review board rules, owners can take the dispute to district court or arbitration.
  • Ask the Hunt County tax office or the district for the current rate on your address.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can reduce a Greenville tax bill?
sections.html:
Several, and the Comptroller prints the amounts. The Comptroller prints a mandatory school district homestead exemption and lets any taxing unit add a local one. Older and disabled owners get more, and disabled veterans have a scale of their own.

Hunt CAD publishes a page for people who inherited a home, because heirs missing from the recorded deed must document their interest to qualify. A veteran rated 100 percent can receive a total exemption on a residence homestead.

sections.h2: What permits and local rules apply to a Greenville house?
sections.html:
Greenville's Permits and Inspections Division reviews building permit applications and inspects construction on private property. Permit types include residential construction, pools and accessory buildings, along with electrical, mechanical, plumbing, concrete and energy work, and applications go through the city's online permitting portal.

If a deck, garage or addition went up without a permit, tell the buyer and ask the city how to regularize it. Open permits can surface during title work and slow a closing. Ask the city about short-term rentals and rental registration before you advertise a house for lodging; a clear answer from the planning office beats assuming the city has no rule.

sections.h2: What if someone is living in my vacant Greenville house?
sections.html:
For some trespassers, Texas offers a quicker route than eviction court. Property Code chapter 24B allows a removal request to the sheriff or constable when four conditions hold: the person stayed after being told to go, the home was closed to the public, no lawsuit is pending between you, and the person is neither family nor a current or former tenant.

A wrongful removal can lead to a lawsuit against the person who requested it. Former tenants go through justice court instead. Resolve who lives there before you advertise.

faqs.q: Which office appraises property in Greenville, Texas?
faqs.a: The Hunt County Appraisal District appraises property in Hunt County, which includes Greenville. It also runs the homestead exemption portal and the protest process.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to file a homestead exemption in Hunt County?
faqs.a: No. Hunt CAD says it charges nothing for a residential homestead application and warns owners not to pay anyone who mails a request for a fee.

faqs.q: When do Greenville protests have to be filed?
faqs.a: Normally by May 15, with a later cutoff if your notice was delivered after mid-April.

faqs.q: Will repairs on my Greenville house need city permits?
faqs.a: Yes for most structural, electrical, plumbing and mechanical work. The city's Permits and Inspections Division reviews applications through its online portal.

faqs.q: May I sell a Greenville house the lender has threatened to foreclose on?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the sale closes ahead of the auction. Texas auctions take place on a month's first Tuesday after a notice of sale at least 21 days earlier.
